memory_update.text: LITE should remain a reference leader for InP lasers, EMLs, datacenter transceivers, and AI optics capacity; less useful as an underfollowed alpha candidate after market recognition.

AAOI is a direct pure-play optical transceiver candidate with concrete 800G/1.6T hyperscaler order evidence; follow-up must test customer concentration, shipment conversion, capacity, and margin quality.
FN is a hidden manufacturing/optical packaging beneficiary; classify as second-order supply-chain capacity exposure rather than branded AI optics product leader.

POET is a speculative shadow candidate in optical engines and optical interposer technology; survival in later layers requires hard evidence of production revenue, qualified customers, and balance-sheet runway.

Need a later pass for non-U.S.-listed but important optical transceiver and InP wafer players such as Innolight, Eoptolink, TFC, IQE, Accelink, and other Asia/Europe suppliers, because the current pass is constrained to US-listed companies.

AAOI should remain in the Layer 1 universe as a direct underfollowed optical transceiver candidate with explicit 1.6T hyperscaler order evidence, but survival depends on shipment conversion, customer concentration risk, and margin follow-through.

TSEM is a high-priority underfollowed silicon-photonics capacity candidate because signed SiPho contracts and customer prepayments may indicate foundry-capacity scarcity tied to 1.6T/NPO/CPO optical networking.
VIAV belongs in the discovery lane as a second-order optical test and qualification vendor; the key evidence gap is materiality of 1.6T AI optical testing within total company revenue.

For AI optical networking, the likely chokepoint map should include pluggable transceivers, InP/EML lasers, silicon-photonics foundry capacity, external laser sources, photonic packaging, and 800G/1.6T validation equipment.

Need a later Layer 1C/2 pass to separate optical-component suppliers with true AI datacenter revenue from legacy telecom/CATV optics, because the same product labels can hide very different demand and margin profiles.
COHR should remain the reference anchor for AI optical components because it discloses a broad 800G/1.6T, CPO, silicon photonics, EML/VCSEL, OCS, and InP-related roadmap.

FN is a second-order optical manufacturing and advanced packaging candidate; the key verification path is customer concentration plus datacom/datacenter interconnect mix rather than generic EMS revenue.

VIAV is a test/certification-gate candidate for AI datacenter Ethernet/optical validation; the next layer should test whether AI-driven 800G/1.6T demand is material versus legacy telecom test exposure.

AXTI is an InP wafer substrate candidate inside the preferred market-cap range; it needs stronger evidence tying revenue to qualified AI/datacenter optical customers and not just broad China optical demand.

POET and AAOI were not included in the final four due to candidate limit and evidence-quality/attention tradeoffs. POET may be a speculative_shadow optical-engine name; AAOI is a direct transceiver name but appears to have become higher-attention and larger-cap by the 2026-06-10 snapshot.

VECO should be tracked as an underfollowed upstream InP laser capacity equipment candidate for AI optical interconnects; key follow-up is backlog conversion and concentration among optical laser manufacturers.
VIAV maps to the optical/network validation chokepoint rather than the module BOM; track whether 1.6T/800G AI data-center test products become material in orders and revenue.
POET remains a speculative-shadow photonic integration candidate: strong node relevance but survival depends on customer qualification, volume shipments, manufacturing yield, and cash runway.

For this node, underfollowed exposure is shifting from obvious transceiver vendors toward InP laser tools, optical test/validation, outsourced precision manufacturing, and wafer-level photonic integration platforms.

Several formerly underfollowed optical names have re-rated above the preferred $300M-$10B range by 2026-06-10, so future Layer 1B passes should emphasize revenue materiality and qualification evidence over market-cap size alone.

node: AI optical networking components and photonics supply chain
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for AI optical networking and photonics. The strongest direct exposures in this pass are optical transceiver/component vendors, advanced laser/InP device suppliers, optical contract manufacturing, and early-stage optical-engine platforms. This is not a recommendation list; it is a Layer 1B research universe. The two-lane funnel keeps Lumentum as a reference product leader while prioritizing less obvious or more narrowly exposed names such as Applied Optoelectronics, Fabrinet, and POET Technologies for follow-up evidence checks. Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around AI optical networking components, emphasizing direct transceiver suppliers, silicon-photonics foundry capacity, and optical-network test vendors. The discovery lane is strongest in AAOI, TSEM, and VIAV because each sits one step away from the obvious AI switch/ASIC vendors and has explicit 800G/1.6T AI data-center language. COHR is included as a reference anchor because it is a better-known vertically integrated photonics supplier and helps benchmark what the market may already recognize. Expanded the AI optical networking components node with a two-lane universe: one reference anchor and three underfollowed/smaller discovery names. The strongest direct chokepoint exposures found in this pass are optical manufacturing/packaging, 800G/1.6T optical test, InP wafer substrates, and optical-engine integration. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the US-listed universe around AI optical networking beyond obvious switch/ASIC leaders.
